demographics.trauma_type: Accidentally caused serious injury to another

Maladaptive Strategies.value: Being emotionally close or intimate with others
Dates or anniversaries connected to the event
become overly compliant when feeling threatened

Threat.value: I am unable to relax even when I know I am in a safe place
Having strong negative feelings such as fear, horror, anger, guilt, or shame
Being superalert or watchful or on guard

Memory.value: My memories of the frightening event are mostly pictures or images.
When I remember the event I feel overwhelming grief
When I remember the event I feel intense guilt

Negative Appraisals.value: The event happened because of the way I acted
I can't stop bad things from happening to me

issues.item: Animal Phobia: Talks or photos about snakes
issues.explanation: For a trauma of accidentally causing serious injury to another, a snake-specific trigger is hard to reconcile unless the accident itself involved snakes, which is not otherwise reflected anywhere in the profile. The other triggers (intrusive thoughts, loud noises) are generic and plausible, but this item appears trauma-incongruent rather than merely unusual.

issues.item: Betrayal: I was betrayed by someone I trusted
issues.explanation: A core appraisal of betrayal by a trusted person is difficult to fit with the indexed trauma of accidentally causing serious injury to another, and it is not supported by the other nodes. The profile otherwise centers on guilt, danger, and dysregulated recall/avoidance, not interpersonal betrayal. This makes the item clinically incoherent with the trauma narrative and cross-node formulation.

Alcohol smell is a hard-to-explain trigger for a trauma described as accidentally causing serious injury to another, given the rest of the profile does not reference alcohol, intoxication, bars, or a vehicle/crash context involving alcohol. It reads disconnected from the stated trauma and the other trigger/memory items.

issues.item: Threat: Avoid Unfamiliar Places: I avoid going to unfamiliar places because I cannot assess the danger
issues.explanation: Avoiding unfamiliar places due to inability to assess danger fits a generalized assault/hypervigilance profile more than guilt-based PTSD after accidentally injuring someone. In this profile, the threat items center on broad environmental danger rather than reminders of having harmed another, which is poorly aligned with the trauma type and with the appraisal/memory content dominated by self-blame and grief.

issues.item: Threat: Scanning Exits: I scan for exits as soon as I enter any room or building
issues.explanation: Scanning exits on entering any room similarly suggests pervasive anticipation of external attack. That is difficult to reconcile with the rest of the profile, which is centered on responsibility for injuring another person rather than being endangered by other people or places.

issues.item: Threat: Scanning Exits: I scan for exits as soon as I enter any room or building
issues.explanation: Scanning for exits in every room/building suggests a danger formulation centered on ongoing external attack or entrapment, which is hard to reconcile with the indexed trauma of accidentally causing serious injury to another person. For this trauma type, threat is more plausibly guilt, loss of control, or fear of causing harm again rather than pervasive escape-oriented hypervigilance.

issues.item: Negative Appraisals: Can't Rely on Others: I can't rely on other people
issues.explanation: 'I can't rely on other people' is weakly anchored to the rest of the profile. The appraisals, memories, and triggers are dominated by self-blame, bodily mistrust, crash imagery, and grief about having injured someone. A global interpersonal mistrust appraisal is not impossible, but here it does not connect well to the accident-caused-harm formulation and lacks support from the other selected items.

issues.item: Negative Appraisals: Body Unreliable: I can no longer trust my own body
issues.explanation: 'Body Unreliable' fits trauma involving bodily injury/physical vulnerability more than the indexed trauma here (accidentally causing serious injury to another). With the rest of the profile centered on guilt and responsibility, this appraisal stands out as poorly matched to trauma type unless there is additional unreported personal injury.

issues.item: Memory: Emotionless Recall: Sometimes I can recall what happened but feel completely numb, as if it happened to a stranger
issues.explanation: Within the Memory node, 'Emotionless Recall' and 'Grief on Recall' can both occur at times, but as the only affective memory items they pull in opposite directions (detached numbness versus overwhelming grief) and are not well integrated by the rest of the profile.

issues.item: Memory: Grief on Recall: When I remember the event I feel overwhelming grief
issues.explanation: 'Crash Imagery: Cars hit by accident' is overly specific to a motor-vehicle collision. The trauma type is only 'accidentally caused serious injury to another'; without any indication this was a car accident, this trigger is too specific and may not match the trauma.

issues.item: Triggers: Crash Imagery: Cars hit by accident
issues.explanation: 'Avoid Intimacy' is not impossible, but in this profile it lacks support from the other selected items. The appraisals, threat, and memory content are centered on guilt, vigilance, and accident reminders rather than interpersonal closeness, so this strategy feels weakly connected compared with the strongly linked nodes in the formulation.
